meta.titre: Cell Structure: membranes, organelles and magnification

sections.contenu_markdown: Every food you buy at Mokolo market, from a tomato to a piece of meat, is made of cells, and every disease treated at the Yaounde Central Hospital involves cells that stop working properly. To study them, biologists use microscopes and describe the structures inside cells with great precision. At GCE Advanced Level you are asked for the exact structure and function of the cell membrane and organelles, for comparisons between plant, animal and bacterial cells, and for calculations of magnification and real size from micrographs.

items: All living organisms are made of cells, and a cell is the basic unit of structure and function.
Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole, which animal cells lack.
1 millimetre (mm) is 1000 micrometres ($\mu$m) and 1 micrometre is 1000 nanometres (nm).

sections.titre: Membranes, organelles and the scale of cells
sections.contenu_markdown:
**The plasma membrane (fluid mosaic model).** The membrane is a **phospholipid bilayer** with the hydrophilic heads facing the water on both sides and the hydrophobic tails inside. **Cholesterol** sits between the phospholipids and regulates fluidity. **Intrinsic (integral) proteins** are embedded in the bilayer and many span it completely; they form **channels** and **carrier proteins** for transport, act as **receptors** for hormones and as **enzymes**. **Extrinsic (peripheral) proteins** lie on one surface only. **Glycoproteins and glycolipids** have carbohydrate chains that act in cell recognition. The membrane is fluid because phospholipids and proteins can move sideways, and it is a mosaic because of the pattern of proteins.

**Eukaryotic organelles.**

| Structure | Structure and function |
|---|---|
| Nucleus | Double membrane (nuclear envelope) with pores; contains **chromatin** (DNA wrapped around histone proteins, condensing into chromosomes at division) and a nucleolus that makes ribosomal RNA; controls the cell |
| Mitochondrion | Double membrane, inner membrane folded into cristae; matrix with 70S ribosomes and circular DNA; site of aerobic respiration |
| Chloroplast | Double membrane, stacks of thylakoids (grana) in a stroma; site of photosynthesis |
| Rough ER | Flattened sacs studded with 80S ribosomes; makes and transports proteins |
| Smooth ER | No ribosomes; makes lipids and steroids |
| Golgi apparatus | Stack of flattened sacs; modifies, packages and secretes proteins and forms lysosomes |
| Lysosome | Single membrane, hydrolytic enzymes; digests worn-out organelles and foreign material |
| Ribosome | Not membrane-bound; made of RNA and protein, site of protein synthesis |
| Cell wall (plants) | Cellulose; gives support and prevents bursting |

**Prokaryote and eukaryote.** Bacterial cells have no nucleus (a circular DNA molecule with no histones lies free in the cytoplasm), no membrane-bound organelles, smaller **70S** ribosomes and a wall of murein. Eukaryotic cells have **80S** ribosomes in the cytoplasm.

**Microscopy.** **Magnification** is how many times larger the image is than the object; **resolution** is the smallest distance at which two points can be seen as separate. The light microscope resolves roughly 200 nm; the transmission electron microscope resolves about 0.5 nm, so it shows ribosomes, membranes and cristae.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the length on a micrograph and the magnification (or a scale bar) are given.
variantes.contenu_markdown: $$M=\dfrac{I}{A}$$ where $I$ is the image size and $A$ the actual size, both in the **same unit**. Rearranged: $A=\dfrac{I}{M}$ and $I=A\times M$. Convert first: 1 mm $=1000\ \mu\text{m}$ and 1 $\mu$m $=1000$ nm. With a scale bar, measure the bar on the picture and divide by the length it represents to obtain $M$.

variantes.nom: Comparing plant, animal and bacterial cells
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for similarities or differences between types of cells.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Plant cells have a cellulose wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole bounded by the tonoplast; animal cells have centrioles and no wall or chloroplasts and store glycogen rather than starch. Bacteria are much smaller (about 1 to 5 $\mu$m), have a murein wall, a circular chromosome and plasmids, and 70S ribosomes. Mitochondria and chloroplasts are about the size of bacteria and contain 70S ribosomes and circular DNA, which is evidence that they arose from engulfed prokaryotes.

sections.enonce_markdown: An electron micrograph of a liver cell shows a mitochondrion. The image of the mitochondrion measures 45 mm in length and the magnification of the micrograph is $\times 15\,000$. Calculate the actual length of the mitochondrion in micrometres and in nanometres, and name the structure by which its inner membrane increases the surface for respiration.

etapes.justification: The magnification relates the image size to the actual size.

etapes.action: Convert the image size to micrometres.
etapes.justification: The answer is to be in micrometres, and 1 mm is 1000 $\mu$m.
Divide the image length by the magnification.
The inner membrane of the mitochondrion is folded.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The folds are the **cristae**; they carry the enzymes and carriers of the electron transport chain.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The mitochondrion is 3.0 $\mu$m (3000 nm) long, which is typical, and its cristae increase the surface for ATP production.

items.erreur_markdown: Dividing the image size in millimetres by the magnification and giving the answer in micrometres.
items.pourquoi_faux: The image size and the actual size are in the same unit only if the units are converted first. 45 mm divided by 15 000 gives 0.003 mm, not 0.003 $\mu$m.
items.correction_markdown: Convert 45 mm to 45 000 $\mu$m before dividing; or give the answer as 0.003 mm $=3\ \mu$m.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that magnification and resolution mean the same thing.
items.pourquoi_faux: Magnification only makes the image bigger; resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points. A highly magnified image can still be blurred.
items.correction_markdown: Define resolution as the minimum distance between two points that can still be seen as separate; the electron microscope has the better resolution.

items.erreur_markdown: Stating that intrinsic proteins lie on the surface of the membrane.
items.pourquoi_faux: Intrinsic proteins are embedded in the bilayer, often spanning it. It is the extrinsic proteins that lie on one surface.
items.correction_markdown: Say that intrinsic proteins span the bilayer and form channels and carriers; extrinsic proteins are on the surface.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that all cells have 80S ribosomes and a nucleus.
items.pourquoi_faux: Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes and no nucleus. Mitochondria and chloroplasts of eukaryotes also have 70S ribosomes.
items.correction_markdown: State that 80S ribosomes are found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells; bacteria have 70S ribosomes.

items.enonce_markdown: The image of a bacterial cell on a photograph is 60 mm long. The real cell is 4.0 $\mu$m long. Calculate the magnification.

A micrograph carries a scale bar of 20 mm which is labelled as representing 2 $\mu$m. A chloroplast in the same micrograph measures 70 mm in length. (a) Calculate the magnification. (b) Calculate the actual length of the chloroplast in micrometres.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The bar measures 20 mm $= 20\,000\ \mu$m on the picture and represents 2 $\mu$m, so $M = \dfrac{20\,000}{2} =$ **$\times 10\,000$**.

(b) $A = \dfrac{I}{M} = \dfrac{70 \times 1000}{10\,000} =$ **7 $\mu$m**.

items.enonce_markdown: A light micrograph of a plant cell has a magnification of $\times 800$. The diameter of the cell measures 56 mm and the diameter of its nucleus measures 11.2 mm. (a) Calculate the actual diameter of the cell and of the nucleus in micrometres. (b) Express the nucleus diameter as a percentage of the cell diameter. (c) The light microscope resolves about 200 nm and the transmission electron microscope about 0.5 nm. By what factor is the resolution of the electron microscope better? (d) Explain why ribosomes cannot be seen with a light microscope.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Cell: $\dfrac{56 \times 1000}{800} =$ **70 $\mu$m**. Nucleus: $\dfrac{11.2 \times 1000}{800} =$ **14 $\mu$m**.

(b) $\dfrac{14}{70}\times 100 =$ **20%**.

(c) $\dfrac{200}{0.5} =$ **400 times** better.

(d) A ribosome is only about 20 to 30 nm across, much smaller than the 200 nm limit of resolution of the light microscope, so it cannot be distinguished as a separate structure; it needs the electron microscope.

items_markdown: The plasma membrane is a fluid mosaic: a phospholipid bilayer with cholesterol, intrinsic proteins that span it (channels, carriers, receptors, enzymes) and extrinsic proteins on the surface.
Chromatin is the complex of DNA and histone proteins in the nucleus; it condenses into chromosomes during cell division.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts have double membranes, circular DNA and 70S ribosomes; eukaryotic cytoplasm has 80S ribosomes.
Prokaryotes have no nucleus, no membrane-bound organelles, a murein wall and 70S ribosomes.
$M=\dfrac{I}{A}$: convert image and actual size to the same unit first (1 mm $=1000\ \mu$m, 1 $\mu$m $=1000$ nm).
Resolution, not magnification, decides what detail can be seen; the electron microscope resolves far finer detail than the light microscope.
